verdicts.evidence:
Direct students' attention to the Noticing and Wondering anchor chart.
- Review what students had noticed and wondered about the sun, moon, and stars during Unit 1 by reading the chart aloud.
- Invite students to turn to an elbow partner and talk after providing 30 seconds of wait time for each of the following questions:
- 'What are some new things you notice about the sun?' (Student responses will vary.)
- 'What are new questions or wonders you have about the sun?' (Student responses will vary.)
- Refocus whole group and call students to share out.
- As students share out, clarify and capture their ideas on the Noticing and Wondering anchor chart, writing down the language they use as accurately as possible.
verdicts.rationale: Students actively use some comprehension strategies (integrating prior knowledge, making inferences, and determining word meanings) during and after read-alouds. Other strategies (purpose-setting by students, monitoring, skimming, summarizing, predicting) are not evidenced.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text:
Engage with a range of complex texts for a variety of tasks and purposes, accessing and using strategies for comprehension before, during, and after reading as part of the meaning-making process.
Comprehension strategies are tools that students should develop throughout their K-12 education as they work to interpret increasingly complex texts. The effectiveness of these strategies depends largely on the texts themselves, the reasons students engage with them, and the preferences and knowledge bases of individual students. For these reasons, students should receive instruction in a variety of comprehension strategies. Students should learn to select and apply strategies flexibly in order to make sense of the text and accomplish their goals.
